title: The Super Narrow Shop Crime Scene
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Inspector Megure, Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The unrelated tag-scene subplot at the very end (a lawsuit involving an 'Atsuko-san') is a different, unconnected case-of-the-week fragment and is excluded entirely. Old lower-fidelity file (cases/ep634...) got the culprit (Shinohara), weapon trick (removable Japanese-knife handle through a rusty wall gap), and swivel-chair repositioning right -- no reversal needed here. What it missed: Shinohara's actual motive (the hostess had been coercing him into stealing high-end produce from the fish market and threatened to expose the thefts if he quit, not mere resentment at being 'forced into escalating theft' with no coercion mechanism specified) and it collapsed the two red-herring suspects' distinct motives (Ougi's debt to the hostess; Nakamura's embezzlement-blackmail) down into a single generic `knows` edge each, plus it used now-deprecated `event` nodes for the murder and the body's repositioning. case_type: murder.

attrs.note: one-person-wide passage running along the bar's back wall

attrs.faucet: broken, sprays water on its own

objects.name: Rusty gap in the back wall

attrs.detail: narrow crack in the iron-plate patching, wide enough for a bare blade

attrs.records: Nakamura's monthly 100,000-yen payments; Shinohara's fish deliveries

attrs.detail: matching bottle on the high shelf had visibly been moved

attrs.mechanism: spins on impact; turned the victim's collapsing body to face the counter

clues.desc: Rust on Shinohara's ATM envelope matches the rusty back-wall gap, not anything on his ATM route -- contradicts his alibi of never returning to the bar.
An unused brandy glass sits on the cutting board though none of the three customers ordered brandy -- implies a phoned-in fake order used to lure the hostess to the wall.

The body was found facing the counter though stabbed near the back wall -- explained by the swivel chair spinning on impact, so the wall-stabbing method isn't contradicted by the body's final position.

edges.detail: used a kind facade getting him the fish market job to make him steal high-end produce; threatened to expose him if he quit
discovered his embezzlement and demanded monthly payments to stay silent
phoned in a fake brandy order from the back alley to draw her against the wall

edges.method: knife blade, handle removed, thrust through the rusty back-wall gap from the alley

edges.detail: slipped the handle back onto the blade while pretending to check on the collapsed victim, disturbing the scene
used the ATM trip/receipt to make the wall-side murder look impossible in the five-minute window

edges.motive_type: debt_collection_dispute (red herring, questioned first for lingering behind)
blackmail_over_embezzlement (red herring, questioned second over ledger payments)
